newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala's Zapata urges investor-friendly laws.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala's Zapata urges investor-friendly laws.

text.p: The head of Guatemala's central bank said on Thursday the country needs new legislation on energy and telecommunications to attract investors.
"Investors are waiting for laws that give certainty as far as handling of the energy and telecommunications sectors," Willy Zapata, president of the Banco de Guatemala, told reporters.

According to Zapata, without new legislation clarifying the rules of the game, Guatemala cannot compete with other Latin American countries trying to attract foreign businesses to buy industries being shed by governments.
The administration's majority National Advancement Party (PAN) has presented in Congress energy and telecommunications bills that would privatize and open up markets in both areas.
The energy law went back to the drawing board in September when it did not get the two-thirds voted it needed to pass.

PAN legislators removed a part of the bill that would have created an automonous commission to oversee production and distribution of electricity. The new version of the bill needs a simple majority vote to pass, but a block of minority parties is pushing for further rewrites.
Congress began floor debates on a telecommunications bill this week.
